ruling: - **R31. A builder resolves a test merge conflict; a check proves no test was lost.** Owner 11:02 CST Nov 11, box answer: "as long as it's well defined and doesn't create loop holes builder plus check definitely seems ideal no?"; and in chat: "yea that check should just protect it as the hand off happens usper often and it's for sure a point of contetnion". It changes page items 420 a (Nov 8 10:05 CST) and 437 a (Nov 8 12:16 CST) in decision builders-cannot-edit-tests. Today a test conflict in a merge stops the builder; a fresh test-author takes the whole merge, and a review round follows. The outcome those rulings protect stays: no side's tests are silently dropped. A check now protects it, and the builder resolves the merge. The check reads test files with the language's own parser. At the merge commit it refuses each of these: 1. A test case from either parent is missing, renamed or moved to another file. 2. A test case's body differs from both parents' versions. 3. A skip or expected-fail mark, or a changed assertion, that neither parent had. 4. New test content that neither parent had. That stays a test-author's work. 5. A change to test config beyond one parent's version, or any change to a mutation test. Page item 447 a (owner 2026-11-08 17:19 CST) stands: a merge that conflicts in a mutation test still goes to a test-author. Each case is shown red on a dropped or weakened test before the route opens. Until then the old route stays. It changes a guard, so the rounds and the net-value rule apply. Home: decision builders-cannot-edit-tests, rewritten in place. Beside it, the same root (triage 11:26 CST Nov 11, from an incident the owner shared in another repo): a test-author briefed to write red checks needed new tooling, was refused, and had to ask the owner. Step brief-role-scope-check catches a brief whose paths do not fit its role at spawn, and sends tooling to a builder first, whose red run is its proof. Owner feedback 12:57 CST Nov 11 (a tile-windows coordinator, relayed by the coordinator 13:00 CST) widens that step: four more incidents, and a refusal for a resume whose worktree is gone.
